note: All 'teams' fields below were produced by calling the UNMODIFIED production functions app.matching._greedy_build -> _two_opt_improve -> _maximin_improve (the same sequence app/matching.py:601-603 uses for POST /teams/generate in 'behavioral' mode) against each dataset.

ability_diversity.note: Uses competence_signature.experience_level (beginner/intermediate/advanced) as an ability PROXY on a 0-2 ordinal scale — the schema has no validated ability or performance measure (e.g. GPA, prior-course grade). Treat as a working hypothesis pending real outcome data. See ability_balance() for the newer [0.0, 1.0] ability_score-based view (Part 3), which prefers a directly-recorded score and reports between-team comparisons too.

ability_balance.note: mean_ability/ability_range/ability_variance use ability_score when a student has one, falling back to experience_level (beginner/intermediate/advanced -> 0.0/0.5/1.0) otherwise — see app.matching._student_ability_score. 'Balanced ability' is a research hypothesis, not a validated target — see AbilityConfig's docstring.

familiarity_density.note: Student model (app/models.py) has no familiarity/prior-contact field. Would need e.g. Student.prior_teammates: List[str] or a separate FamiliarityDB edge table (student_a, student_b, strength) populated from a roster survey or LMS co-enrollment history. See research_alignment_audit.md §4.

clique_concentration.note: No friend-group / social-cluster data available. Would need either self-reported prior-group data at onboarding or a derived clustering over a familiarity graph. See research_alignment_audit.md §4.

familiarity_balance.note: density is the mean familiarity strength over KNOWN pairs only; a pair with no recorded FamiliarityDB row is excluded from the average entirely, not treated as 0.0. 'largest_connected_cluster' is computed from the TEAM-INDUCED subgraph (edges between this team's own members only, at/above clique_edge_threshold=0.5) — a connected COMPONENT, not necessarily a clique (a chain or star can form one cluster without every pair being directly connected; see its cohesion fields to tell them apart). band_status is 'not_applicable' for teams with 0-1 members, 'insufficient_data' when known_pair_coverage is below minimum_known_pair_coverage=0.5 (not enough recorded data among these specific teammates to trust a density judgment — isolated_members and the cluster above remain populated from whatever known edges DO exist, only the band classification is suppressed), otherwise below/within/above the configured band. Neither the band bounds nor the pair/cluster/coverage thresholds are scientifically established for this population — see FamiliarityConfig's docstring.

preference_satisfaction.note: No preference data collected anywhere in the pipeline (models.py has no `preferred_teammates` / `avoid_teammates` field, and no assessment scenario asks for it). Would need a ranked-preference field on Student or a dedicated PreferenceDB table, e.g. (student_id, preferred_id, rank). See research_alignment_audit.md §7.

blocking_moves_score_based.note: Score-based proxy: flags swaps that would raise BOTH teams' aggregate scores post-hoc. True stability requires individual preference data (see blocking_pairs_preference_based).

blocking_pairs_preference_based.note: Requires per-student ranked teammate/team preferences, which the schema does not currently collect. See research_alignment_audit.md §7 for the proposed field.

preference_satisfaction.note: satisfaction_score is None (MISSING, not 0.0) for a student with zero 'prefer' entries -- excluded from mean/min/max/stdev/fraction_with_at_least_one_preferred_teammate. A student WITH entries none of which matched their team scores exactly 0.0 -- a real outcome, distinct from having no opinion. Ties/indifference are expressed by multiple entries sharing the same rank (or all left unranked); see this module's tier-scoring docstring for the exact formula. Avoidance is honored UNILATERALLY -- a violation is counted whenever EITHER teammate in a pair named the other as an 'avoid' target, regardless of reciprocity.

stability.note: is_stable reflects the 'blocking_swap' definition (see app/matching.py's preference-framework module docstring for all three formal definitions and why blocking_swap is the documented default). The other two counts are always computed as supplementary diagnostics regardless of which definition is authoritative here.

constraint_violations.note: Reuses app.matching._check_floor_violations() directly (read-only import) so this harness evaluates exactly the constraint the production algorithm enforces, not a reimplementation of it.

ability_diversity.note: Uses competence_signature.experience_level (beginner/intermediate/advanced) as an ability PROXY on a 0-2 ordinal scale — the schema has no validated ability or performance measure (e.g. GPA, prior-course grade). Treat as a working hypothesis pending real outcome data. See ability_balance() for the newer [0.0, 1.0] ability_score-based view (Part 3), which prefers a directly-recorded score and reports between-team comparisons too.

ability_balance.correlation_note: Not computed: needs >=3 teams with non-constant mean ability AND non-constant skill coverage to be meaningful (this partition has 2 team(s) with a resolvable mean ability).
ability_balance.note: mean_ability/ability_range/ability_variance use ability_score when a student has one, falling back to experience_level (beginner/intermediate/advanced -> 0.0/0.5/1.0) otherwise — see app.matching._student_ability_score. 'Balanced ability' is a research hypothesis, not a validated target — see AbilityConfig's docstring.

familiarity_density.note: Student model (app/models.py) has no familiarity/prior-contact field. Would need e.g. Student.prior_teammates: List[str] or a separate FamiliarityDB edge table (student_a, student_b, strength) populated from a roster survey or LMS co-enrollment history. See research_alignment_audit.md §4.

clique_concentration.note: No friend-group / social-cluster data available. Would need either self-reported prior-group data at onboarding or a derived clustering over a familiarity graph. See research_alignment_audit.md §4.

familiarity_balance.note: density is the mean familiarity strength over KNOWN pairs only; a pair with no recorded FamiliarityDB row is excluded from the average entirely, not treated as 0.0. 'largest_connected_cluster' is computed from the TEAM-INDUCED subgraph (edges between this team's own members only, at/above clique_edge_threshold=0.5) — a connected COMPONENT, not necessarily a clique (a chain or star can form one cluster without every pair being directly connected; see its cohesion fields to tell them apart). band_status is 'not_applicable' for teams with 0-1 members, 'insufficient_data' when known_pair_coverage is below minimum_known_pair_coverage=0.5 (not enough recorded data among these specific teammates to trust a density judgment — isolated_members and the cluster above remain populated from whatever known edges DO exist, only the band classification is suppressed), otherwise below/within/above the configured band. Neither the band bounds nor the pair/cluster/coverage thresholds are scientifically established for this population — see FamiliarityConfig's docstring.

blocking_moves_score_based.note: Score-based proxy: flags swaps that would raise BOTH teams' aggregate scores post-hoc. True stability requires individual preference data (see blocking_pairs_preference_based).

preference_satisfaction.note: satisfaction_score is None (MISSING, not 0.0) for a student with zero 'prefer' entries -- excluded from mean/min/max/stdev/fraction_with_at_least_one_preferred_teammate. A student WITH entries none of which matched their team scores exactly 0.0 -- a real outcome, distinct from having no opinion. Ties/indifference are expressed by multiple entries sharing the same rank (or all left unranked); see this module's tier-scoring docstring for the exact formula. Avoidance is honored UNILATERALLY -- a violation is counted whenever EITHER teammate in a pair named the other as an 'avoid' target, regardless of reciprocity.

stability.note: is_stable reflects the 'blocking_swap' definition (see app/matching.py's preference-framework module docstring for all three formal definitions and why blocking_swap is the documented default). The other two counts are always computed as supplementary diagnostics regardless of which definition is authoritative here.

constraint_violations.note: Reuses app.matching._check_floor_violations() directly (read-only import) so this harness evaluates exactly the constraint the production algorithm enforces, not a reimplementation of it.

part_6_5.note: Part 6.5 validated the Part 6 profile system before a real student study. See research_alignment_audit.md Part 6.5 section and docs/performance.md / docs/profile_distinctness.md for full narrative. Every sub-key here is the raw output of the evaluation script named, generated in this session.

performance_benchmark.note: Median of 3 repeats per (roster size, profile), deterministic synthetic rosters (evaluation.benchmark_profiles._synthetic_roster), wall-clock via time.perf_counter() around _greedy_build -> _two_opt_improve -> _maximin_improve -> _run_optional_passes (the exact sequence generate_teams() calls). NOT cProfile-instrumented (profiling adds its own overhead).

collapse_to_legacy_check.description: research_balanced's own default settings against legacy, on the seed roster — checks whether enabling every pass with conservative defaults ever produces a DIFFERENT result from simply not running them.

experiment_readiness_example.distinct_enough_caveat: This threshold is a CONFIGURABLE STUDY-DESIGN CHOICE (ReadinessConfig.min_comembership_distance_for_distinct_conditions), not a validated statistical cutoff for 'different enough' — no such universal cutoff is claimed.
